summary: Iteration 3 — Stripe sandbox donations feature end-to-end verified. Backend: 5/5 new pytest checks in test_donations.py pass (invalid package_id -> 400; valid don_10 -> checkout.stripe.com URL + session_id + Mongo record with payment_status=pending/status=initiated; GET /api/payments/status/{sid} returns pending for unpaid session and 404 for unknown; GET /api/donations/total counts only payment_status=paid, verified by inserting/removing a fake paid record). Frontend: initial map load shows world view (zoom 2, center [22,5], all continents visible in one screen), header donation-counter present with '€' symbol, 100 donate-btn-<id> buttons in project list, DonateModal opens with all 5 preset amounts (5/10/25/50/100), popup markup contains popup-donate-btn wired to window.__biDonate, EN/FR toggle works ('Donner' in FR), audit/settings panels open. E2E paid-return flow simulated: created real Stripe sandbox session, marked it paid directly in Mongo, visited /payment/success?session_id=..., PaymentReturn modal polled and displayed payment-success-msg ('Donation confirmed!'), header counter updated to '25 € donations (1)'. Test data cleaned afterwards (donations/total back to 0.00 / 0). Swarm NOT redeployed and projects NOT deleted per instructions.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now ~535 lines and mixes projects/swarm/settings/import/manuals/donations/webhook. Strongly recommend splitting into routers/ package (projects.py, swarm.py, settings.py, donations.py) plus a webhooks.py; readability is degrading fast.

DONATION_PACKAGES are hard-coded server side but also duplicated in frontend Donations.js PACKAGES. Consider exposing GET /api/donations/packages so amounts stay in sync (single source of truth) and the frontend can be internationalised without touching JS.
payment_status endpoint silently swallows all Stripe SDK errors with bare except; a genuine Stripe outage will be indistinguishable from 'not paid yet'. Log the exception at minimum.

No idempotency key sent when creating Stripe checkout sessions — a double-click on a Donate amount will create two Mongo payment_transactions rows and two Stripe sessions. Frontend already disables the buttons while busy, but backend should also enforce a short-lived idempotency guard.

Webhook route /api/webhook/stripe is registered directly on app (not via APIRouter) — inconsistent with the rest of the API and easy to miss when refactoring. Move it to a webhooks router while keeping the /api prefix.

PaymentReturn polling stops after ~10 attempts (20s) with no user-facing retry. For real Stripe webhooks that can arrive slightly late this may briefly show 'timeout' even for successful payments; consider extending or offering a Refresh button.

Frontend hardcodes the origin for redirect back (window.location.origin) — fine for now but keep in mind that if backend is behind a different host than frontend the origin passed to Stripe should still match the domain the user is on (currently correct).
